summary: An occupational, physical or speech therapist who trains people with paralysis, ALS, stroke or spinal cord injury to use implanted brain-computer interfaces and neurostimulators (today's analogues: BrainGate, Neuralink PRIME, Synchron COMMAND, Blackrock, Onward ARC trials), from decoder calibration sessions to home use and outcome reporting. AI helps most with session planning, analyzing performance logs, trial-grade documentation, plain-language patient and caregiver materials, and keeping up with fast-moving device, regulatory and neural-data-privacy rules.

prompts.title: Calibration session plan
prompts.task: Plan a structured BCI decoder calibration and training session for a specific participant
prompts.prompt: You are an experienced occupational therapist on an implanted BCI team. Plan a [SESSION LENGTH]-minute training session for a participant with [DIAGNOSIS, e.g. C4 SCI / ALS, ALSFRS-R score] using [DEVICE/DECODER TYPE, e.g. intracortical cursor decoder]. Current status: [RECENT PERFORMANCE, e.g. bits/sec, Fitts' law throughput, typing WPM], fatigue pattern [DETAILS], participant goal [GOAL, e.g. independent texting]. Output a table: block, task (e.g. center-out, grid task, copy-typing), duration, rest, success criterion, and what to change if performance drops. Add fatigue and frustration stop rules, and note which steps need the engineer present. Stay within the study protocol [PROTOCOL CONSTRAINTS].
prompts.caution: Session content must stay within the approved IDE/IRB protocol; the study team, not the AI, decides parameter changes.

prompts.title: Performance drop troubleshooting
prompts.task: Work through likely causes when a participant's BCI control degrades
prompts.prompt: Act as a BCI clinical-research therapist reviewing a performance decline. Over [TIME PERIOD], [PARTICIPANT ID] went from [BASELINE METRICS] to [CURRENT METRICS]. Context: days since recalibration [N], sleep/meds/mood changes [NOTES], illness or spasticity [NOTES], setup changes (seating, screen distance, environment) [NOTES], engineer notes on signal quality/channel counts [NOTES]. Produce a ranked differential split into (a) participant/clinical factors, (b) setup and task factors, (c) signal/decoder factors to escalate to engineering. For each, give the quick check I can do in-session and what result would rule it in or out. Flag anything suggesting a medical issue (e.g. infection, seizure activity, neurological change) for immediate physician review.
prompts.caution: Hardware, signal or neurological concerns go to the engineer and study physician; do not adjust implant settings yourself.

prompts.title: Trial session note
prompts.task: Turn raw session notes into a structured research/clinical note
prompts.prompt: You are a documentation assistant for a neural implant rehab study. Convert my raw notes into a session note with headings: Participant ID (de-identified), Date/Session #, Tasks performed, Quantitative results [METRICS], Standardized measures administered (e.g. ARAT, GRASSP, COPM, QUEST) with scores, Participant-reported fatigue/comfort/satisfaction, Adverse events or device issues (stating 'none reported' only if my notes say so), Deviations from protocol, Plan for next session. Keep facts exactly as given; mark missing items as [MISSING] rather than guessing. Raw notes: [PASTE DE-IDENTIFIED NOTES].
prompts.caution: Paste only de-identified data unless your organization has approved the tool for PHI; any adverse event must also go through the formal AE reporting process.

prompts.title: Caregiver home-use guide
prompts.task: Write a plain-language guide for family/caregivers supporting home BCI use
prompts.prompt: Write a plain-language home guide (reading level about grade 6) for caregivers of [PARTICIPANT FIRST NAME OR 'the user'], who uses [DEVICE] at home for [USES, e.g. texting, computer access, wheelchair control]. Base it only on these approved instructions: [PASTE MANUFACTURER/STUDY INSTRUCTIONS]. Sections: daily setup checklist, positioning and charging, signs of tiredness and when to stop, skin/incision or headpiece checks to report, what to do if the system stops working, who to call and when (with [CONTACT NUMBERS]), and respecting the user's privacy and choice to switch it off. Use short bullets and add a one-page quick-reference version.
prompts.caution: Must be checked against the device IFU/study materials and approved by the study team before distribution.

prompts.title: Goal and outcome-measure plan
prompts.task: Map a participant's functional goals to measurable outcomes over a training block
prompts.prompt: Act as a rehabilitation outcomes specialist. My participant has [DIAGNOSIS, LEVEL, TIME SINCE INJURY] and an implant for [FUNCTION, e.g. computer control / spinal stimulation for hand function]. Their priorities (from COPM interview): [GOALS]. Propose a [N]-week plan: for each goal, a SMART objective, the standardized measure that fits (e.g. COPM, GRASSP, ARAT, SCIM III, QUEST, task-specific metrics like WPM), measurement schedule, and a minimal clinically important difference where one is published (say if none exists for this population). Note which outcomes reflect device performance versus real-life participation, and suggest how to capture the participant's own view of benefit.
prompts.caution: Verify MCID values and measure validity in the source literature before relying on them.

prompts.title: Informed-consent and expectations talk
prompts.task: Prepare to discuss realistic expectations and risks with a prospective participant
prompts.prompt: Help me prepare for a conversation with a prospective participant with [CONDITION] considering enrolling in [TRIAL NAME/DEVICE] study. Using only this approved consent summary [PASTE KEY POINTS: procedures, risks, time commitment, explant plan, end-of-study device support], draft: (1) a plain-language talking-points outline, (2) honest answers to likely questions such as 'Will this let me walk/move again?', 'What happens to my data?', 'What if the company stops supporting the device?', and 'Can I withdraw?', (3) signs the person may not understand or may feel pressured, and how to slow down. Avoid overstating benefit; flag any question I should refer to the PI or surgeon.
prompts.caution: Formal consent is obtained by authorized study staff using the IRB-approved form; these are preparation notes only.

prompts.title: Neural data privacy check
prompts.task: Review a planned data use against privacy rules for neural data
prompts.prompt: Act as a privacy-aware clinical research advisor. We want to [PLANNED USE, e.g. share session videos and decoded text logs with a university partner / use a home telemetry app]. Jurisdiction: [STATE/COUNTRY]. Data involved: [DATA TYPES]. Summarize which frameworks likely apply (e.g. HIPAA, Common Rule/IRB consent terms, GDPR special-category data, state neural-data laws such as Colorado's and California's 2024 amendments, Chile's neurorights provisions) and what each would require here. Then list concrete questions for our privacy officer/IRB, risks of re-identification from neural or decoded-speech data, and safeguards. Clearly flag where the law is new, unsettled, or I need legal confirmation.
prompts.caution: Not legal advice; confirm with your privacy officer, IRB and counsel.

prompts.title: Upskilling study plan
prompts.task: Build a learning plan to move from conventional rehab into neural implant work
prompts.prompt: I am a [OT/PT/SLP] with [YEARS] years in [SETTING, e.g. SCI inpatient rehab] and want to work on implanted BCI and neuromodulation teams. Create a 12-week self-study plan covering: basic neurophysiology of motor/speech cortex recording, how intracortical, endovascular (Stentrode) and ECoG approaches differ, decoder calibration concepts, performance metrics (bits/sec, Fitts' law), spinal cord stimulation rehab (e.g. ARC therapy evidence), the FDA's 2021 implanted BCI guidance, IDE/GCP (ISO 14155) basics, and neuroethics. For each week give objectives, 2-3 key sources (landmark papers, guidance documents, BCI Society resources) and a practical exercise. Mark sources I should verify are current.
prompts.caution: Check citations exist and are up to date; the field changes quickly.
